title: Right now my zombie game has one zombie wearing a hundred different faces
author: No-Fee-2707
selftext:
I’ve been working on a zombie survival game with shooting, enemy waves, exploration, and a mostly complete survival loop. I used SeeleAgent to build the current playable version, but testing it has made one problem pretty obvious: most of the zombies behave exactly the same.

They chase the player, get close, and attack. Different appearances help visually, but after a few waves they all feel like the same enemy.

I could add the usual fast zombie, armored zombie, crawler, and screamer, but simply changing health and speed doesn’t seem like enough. I’d rather have enemies that change how the player uses the environment.

Maybe some zombies can climb over obstacles, knock down barricades, crawl through gaps, pull the player off high ground, or force other zombies through blocked paths. That could also make the terrain more useful instead of just being something the player occasionally gets stuck on.

How many distinct zombie types does a survival game actually need? Do you prefer lots of small variations, or a few enemies with clearly different behaviors?

If you could add one zombie type that changes how the player moves or fights, what would it do?

comments.author: imnotabot303
comments.body:
Currently this looks like one of those Steam asset flips from 10 years ago.

I think you need to focus on fixing that camera before you worry about anything else. There's also a a 1001 zombie games so a low quality zombie wave shooter probably isn't going to be very appealing to anyone. You will need to come up with a game mechanic that makes it unique.

Having interesting enemies is going to require unique animations for each type of zombie, unique models and more complex AI systems as in intelligence for NPC control.

replies.author: EC36339
replies.body: The camera glitch is easy to fix and only important when showing off the game to people who have no clue about game development. Anyone else would understand that this is a cosmetic detail that can wait.

replies.author: imnotabot303
replies.body: It's not a cosmetic detail or a glitch, your camera is broken which makes the game unplayable. You either need to fix the camera so it's not constantly going inside geometry or adjust your environment to a more open space so you don't need to worry about it so much.

replies.author: EC36339
replies.body:
1. It is not "my" camera. It is not my game.

2. It is a cosmetic glitch. Important eventually, but not at this stage.

replies.author: imnotabot303
replies.body:
I don't know why you are so defensive. People are offering constructive criticism. When making a game it's important to get the fundamentals solid before thinking about something like enemy AI otherwise you could waste a bunch of time. 

Getting your player and camera controls working and feeling good plus planning and blocking out your levels is one of the first build steps.

I also gave you advice on what you need to do for the zombies. More unique models and animations, better enemy AI and something to make the game feel unique so it's not like the thousands of other basic wave shooters out there.

Look at other successful games. Usually they are going have enemies with different types of attack. Some might have DOT attacks, some might be fast light attacks or slow heavy attacks, some might be single target, some AOE etc.

Usually you would plan this stuff out before even starting to make the game.

replies.author: EC36339
replies.body: It is not my game. I am not OP. Learn to read.

replies.author: imnotabot303
replies.body: Well I confused you with the OP because for some reason you were trying to defend their poor choices so my bad for that but my feedback is still useful for the OP anyway.

replies.author: EC36339
replies.body: That's a lot of words for "I replied without reading".

replies.author: Aromatic-Low-4578
replies.body: Nah, bad cameras have killed tons of games, it's worth tackling early and getting right. It literally frames the entire game.

replies.author: EC36339
replies.body:
It is easy to fix.

It is not important at this stage of development, except for presentation.

Is this so hard to understand or are you just stubborn?

replies.author: Aromatic-Low-4578
replies.body: A video game is *entirely* about presentation, without nailing down the camera mechanics you don't know what anything else in the game looks like to an actual player. You don't know how much detail is needed for models or textures, you don't know how animations read, you don't know if level design is intuitive and interesting.  I could go on but you get the point, unless you're just stubborn.

replies.author: EC36339
replies.body:
Damm, are people stupid on this platform.

Repeat these words after me, slowly:

That
Game

!

Duh!

Jeez, the level of autism here is unbearable

replies.author: Aromatic-Low-4578
replies.body: Ah, personal insults, the last resort of someone who knows they're wrong.  Good luck with your game.

comments.author: NoEye89
comments.body: You killed a 'boss' fell onto the ground, ran around for thirty seconds clipping through every wall imaginable, and then quickly defeated all three bosses in your 'gams'. Sorry, but back to the drawing board on this one.

replies.author: EC36339
replies.body: The camera clipping glitch at least is evidence that the video is real and that actual game development is going on here. It is also easy to fix, not something on which one should judge an entire project that is in progress. It wouldn't be anyone's top priority, except when making a video to show it off, of course.

replies.author: LatentBlade
replies.body: You have to understand people will notice the things that are wrong disproportionately. It took me a minute. I'd say X is not ready yet and they immediately would be like X is not ready. If you want Internet points for progress in a crowded market wait until you don't see things in the clip you know you need to fix.   And then someone will point out something you didn't notice and you have to decide whether they are right or not objectively.

replies.author: EC36339
replies.body:
Of course I understand that people notice the wrong things. That's why I said it matters for presentation. It doesn't matter for development at this time.

Please, do make an effort to read before you reply.

replies.author: LatentBlade
replies.body: I'm trying to tell you it's always presentation. It's not the way I want. It's the way it is. If you can't get through this thread without attitude you're going to have a bad time making a game.

replies.author: EC36339
replies.body: That's nonsense. And I'm tired of repeating myself.

comments.author: gilliganis
comments.body: Based on your gameplay video I would say that the zombie behaviour is currently one of the least of your game’s concerns
